claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is in a solidified solid-solution state.
Removing Co from the alloy alters its short-range chemical order.
The Co-free alloy contains localized short-range-order clusters that act as dislocation-pinning centers.
Short-range ordering increases the alloy's sensitivity to strain rate and temperature.
At low temperatures, short-range ordering delays dislocation unpinning.
Local compositional fluctuations produce enhanced short-range order in the Co-free alloy.
The short-range-order regions in the Co-free alloy pin dislocations more effectively than the ordering present in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
At low temperatures and high strain rates, limited thermal activation makes dislocation motion more strongly impeded.
Stronger impediment of dislocation motion increases yield strength.
Increasing temperature assists dislocation unpinning in the Co-free alloy.
Thermally assisted unpinning reduces the mechanical-response difference between the Co-free alloy and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
At low temperatures, the Co-free alloy will have higher yield strength than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi under otherwise identical conditions.
At low temperatures, the Co-free alloy will have greater strain-rate sensitivity than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
At high temperatures, yield-strength and ductility differences between the Co-free alloy and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi will diminish.
The proposed predictions are bounded to approximately 200–1200 K and strain rates of approximately 10^-4–10^8 s^-1.
Magnetic interactions may also contribute to the mechanical behavior.
